With the formation of the alliance, the world's economy is doing quite a bit better than it has in recent years, despite the continued crises that we face. The various rebuilding efforts are strong, and charitable organizations are seeing continued support from all strata of society.  
  
There have been a few issues with integrating Cantha into global trade networks, as some citizens of New Kaineng are so ridiculously wealthy compared to the average Krytan that it's led to a surge of so-called "tourist pricing."  
  
For example, we interviewed an Awakened merchant on the streets of Amnoon who claimed they were just back from Arborstone. However, reports from Arborstone claimed that same merchant disappeared months ago. Either way, we noticed that they were selling Joko statues at ten times the normal cost. When we inquired about the price increase, they refused to give us a straight answer about the price or their recent travel history.

(This appears to be a fragment of a journal.)

There was a vision.

A promise—that we'd win.

My god is dead. Aurene, gone. The warmth of Balthazar's spirit is now just cold, lifeless crystal. Kralkatorrik took her from me, just as his Brand will soon take this world.

I thought that I had finally found...something. A hope that what I was holding on to was real. That it was pure and good.

Maybe it was.

Maybe what I had for that short time between my lowest point and the end of all things was as good as it will ever get for me.

Or maybe the vision that saw me standing there at her side during the final battle against Kralkatorrik was meant as a warning for me stay away.

There is no solace in what lies ahead. All I can do is look to the past, and I carry it with me wherever I go.

(There appear to have been more pages at one point, but they have been removed.)

Commander,

Here are the known White Mantle hideouts that the Shining Blade continue to monitor for activity. Though none of our spies reported any noteworthy activity the past few months, that doesn't mean that our three White Mantle wouldn't have left ties to their actions at any of the locations. At minimum, it's worth getting a closer look.

Divinity's Reach: In the past, Shining Blade agents have observed White Mantle activity by the gardens in the northeastern corner of Rurikton. As it is near the gates leading to Lake Doric, it continues to be a notorious spot for White Mantle vs. Seraph altercations.

Brisban Wildlands: Their hideout north of this region remains abandoned after we cleaned out one of their cells during that whole Lazarus adventure. However, clusters of the bandits in the Wendon Steps continue to be sympathetic to the White Mantle. They may still harbor the occasional justiciar and their forces. Couldn't hurt to take a look.

Shire of Beetletun: In the northeast corner of Queensdale, the shire situated right outside Caudecus's former estate remains under the Shining Blade's watchful eye. Still, the minister's most loyal servants make pilgrimages to the site, perhaps hoping that against all hope that he may someday return. Pathetic, really... But then again, here we are working with a wizard returned from death. Who are we to judge what's possible? At any rate, I could see any of our three loyalists wanting to remain close to Caudecus this way.

Exactly what should you be looking for at these locations? That, I leave to your judgment... A "you'll know it when you see it" sort of thing. Best of luck, Commander.
